reference.source: Stiehm's Immunologic Disorders / IUIS classification of inborn errors of immunity
clinicalPearls: Characteristic cytopenia pattern is monocytopenia with loss of B lymphocytes, natural killer cells and dendritic cells, producing the descriptive term DCML (dendritic cell, monocyte, B and NK lymphoid) deficiency
Disseminated non-tuberculous mycobacterial infection is a defining feature, hence the MonoMAC designation, alongside severe HPV disease, fungal infection and reactivation of herpesviruses
There is a strong predisposition to myelodysplastic syndrome and acute myeloid leukaemia, which may be the presenting problem in adolescence or adulthood
Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis and progressive interstitial lung disease occur and can dominate the clinical picture
Lymphoedema and sensorineural deafness (Emberger syndrome) represent one recognised presentation of the same gene defect
Inheritance is autosomal dominant with highly variable expressivity and age of onset, and de novo variants are common
The bone marrow is typically hypocellular with dysplasia and characteristic abnormal megakaryocytes even before overt malignancy
Allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation is the only curative option and is often pursued before transformation to leukaemia
reference.pathophysiology: GATA2 encodes a zinc-finger transcription factor essential for the generation and maintenance of haematopoietic stem and progenitor cells and for lymphatic development. Haploinsufficiency from loss-of-function or regulatory variants progressively depletes the stem-cell pool, causing loss of monocytes, dendritic cells, B lymphocytes and natural killer cells while a hypocellular, dysplastic marrow evolves. The immune-cell deficits impair defence against intracellular pathogens such as mycobacteria, papillomavirus and fungi, and the unstable haematopoietic compartment predisposes to clonal evolution, myelodysplasia and acute myeloid leukaemia. Impaired lymphatic development explains the lymphoedema seen in some patients.
additionalDifferentials: Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease (IL-12/IFN-gamma axis defects)
additionalInvestigations: Full blood count with differential showing monocytopenia and cytopenias
Lymphocyte subsets demonstrating loss of B cells, NK cells and dendritic cells
Bone marrow aspirate and trephine with cytogenetics for dysplasia and clonal abnormalities
Serum immunoglobulins and specific antibody responses
GATA2 gene sequencing including non-coding regulatory regions and deletion analysis
High-resolution chest imaging and pulmonary function to assess alveolar proteinosis or interstitial disease
redFlags: Progressive cytopenias or blasts on the film indicating transformation to MDS or AML
Disseminated mycobacterial or invasive fungal infection
Rapidly worsening breathlessness from pulmonary alveolar proteinosis
New or extensive HPV lesions concerning for malignant change
Unexplained lymphoedema with a family history of haematological disease
reference.prognosis: The natural history is progressive, with a high cumulative risk of myelodysplasia and leukaemia and of severe infective and pulmonary complications; timely allogeneic transplantation, ideally before leukaemic transformation, offers the best chance of long-term survival.
pitfalls: Diagnosing MDS or AML in a young person without considering an underlying GATA2 defect that affects donor selection
Overlooking the diagnosis because immunoglobulins are relatively preserved early on
Missing regulatory or deep intronic variants when only coding sequence is analysed
Attributing pulmonary alveolar proteinosis to an autoimmune cause
Failing to screen relatives before using a related haematopoietic stem cell donor
references: Stiehm's Immunologic Disorders in Infants and Children
IUIS Expert Committee classification of inborn errors of immunity
management: Allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation is the only curative therapy and is best undertaken before myelodysplastic or leukaemic transformation
Aggressive treatment of disseminated non-tuberculous mycobacterial infection with combination antimycobacterial therapy, plus antifungal and antiviral cover for opportunistic infection
Surveillance and treatment of human papillomavirus disease, with vaccination and monitoring for malignant transformation
Regular marrow surveillance with cytogenetics for evolving myelodysplasia and acute myeloid leukaemia
Whole-lung lavage and respiratory support for pulmonary alveolar proteinosis, with monitoring of lung function and interstitial disease
Multidisciplinary management including complex lymphoedema care where present
Genetic counselling for autosomal dominant inheritance, cascade family testing and screening of related potential stem cell donors
